summary: How far a piece of work has got, as a ring that fills clockwise from the top: a value out of `max`, a required label, an intent for the thing measured. Determinate only.
useWhen: measurable progress has to fit a square or a line of text — a page header's status, a table cell, beside a step count
one figure is the point of a card — a setup that is 3 of 5 done, a quota at 72% — and a ring with the percentage inside reads at a glance
the work is measurable from the start; it will not begin as an unknown and become a number

useInstead.when: the work cannot be measured — a wait with no fraction
useInstead.why: a ring stuck at 0% says the work has not started; a spinner says it is running and unmeasured

useInstead.when: the work starts unmeasurable and becomes measurable, such as an upload before its size is known
useInstead.why: ProgressBar keeps its node when the value arrives, so the change is announced; swapping a Spinner for a ring remounts it and goes silent

useInstead.when: there is room for a row, or several are compared down a list
useInstead.why: lengths side by side compare at a glance; rings side by side are angles, which people read far less accurately

composition.note: `label` names the work and is required, shown or not. Give `valueText` whenever a count means more than a percentage — "3 of 5 steps done" — and it is both spoken and shown beside the ring. Small sits in a line of text and puts its value beside it; Medium and Large hold the percentage inside.
composition.example: <ProgressRing size="sm" label="Run progress" value={done} max={total} valueText={`${done} of ${total} steps done`} isValueVisible />

sm.use: in a line of text — a header's status, a table cell; its value goes beside it

md.use: the default — a card, with the percentage inside

lg.use: the one figure a card or an empty page is about

success.use: work that finished, where the ring stays on screen as a record

warning.note: warning describes the VALUE, not a failure of the ring

error.use: a quota exceeded, or a job that failed part-way
error.note: reserve this for the measured thing being bad

requires: `label` — it is required, because role="progressbar" announces a number and a number with no noun sounds like information while carrying none
`valueText` when a percentage is not what a person wants read aloud — "3 of 5 steps done"
guarantees: one progressbar named by `label`, shown or not, with `aria-valuenow`, its bounds, and `aria-valuetext` from `valueText`
the drawing and the percentage inside it are hidden from assistive tech: the value is already announced
`value` is held to 0..`max`, and `max={0}` draws an empty ring rather than NaN
the ring fills clockwise from twelve o'clock in every direction; in right to left, only the text beside it moves
"100%" fits inside Medium and Large with room to spare
in forced colours the track is GrayText and the fill Highlight
notes: Not a live region. A value that changes while the reader waits for it belongs in a status message as well — "Indexing finished" — not in a ring that announces every step.
The fill is `surface/*`, as ProgressBar's is, and its track is `surface/muted`.

antiPatterns.dont: <ProgressRing label="Loading" value={0} /> while the total is unknown
antiPatterns.do: <Spinner label="Loading" />, or a ProgressBar with no `value`
antiPatterns.why: a ring at 0% says nothing has happened; unknown progress is a different message

antiPatterns.dont: a column of rings comparing agents' budgets
antiPatterns.why: people compare lengths well and angles badly, so the column hides which is nearest its limit

antiPatterns.do: leave the ring and put the failure in an Alert
antiPatterns.why: intent describes the value being measured; a failed request is a different message
